phases.title: Opening a site
phases.sub: We do these four things once, in this order, for every new site.

phases.title: Running it
phases.sub: Day 0 opens the site. The other three repeat every day it is live.

stages.title: Sourcing
stages.why: We look for the sites that add the kinds of work we need more of, and we get ourselves in the room.
do: We keep a list of the kinds of places we want to film in. We rank it by the task types we need more of, and we think about how the footage will get out.
We reach out through people we know, and we walk in and ask.
Anyone who brings in a site that signs gets a 10% referral reward. Portfolio Managers look for sites for their own books and earn the same reward.
stages.done: We have a meeting booked with someone at the site who can say yes.

stages.title: Closing
stages.owner: Adham and Youssif, with Mano on the paperwork
stages.why: We make the site ours on paper before anyone shows up with a phone.
do: We meet the owner, walk the floor together, and agree on what we film and what we pay.
We sign the participation agreement and agree on the signage and the consent forms.
We set the hours we can be there, who is allowed in, and the safety rules of that site.
stages.done: The agreement is signed, we have confirmed access, and Mano has the payment terms on file.

stages.title: Planning the floor
stages.owner: Mazen, Moharam, and the site's Portfolio Manager
stages.why: We design the operation for this specific floor before Day 0.
do: We walk the whole site. We mark where we record, where we never record, where the power outlets are, and where the equipment will live.
We confirm how the footage gets out: the site's own line, a router, or a run to one of our hubs.
We agree on the safety rules and the protective gear for that floor.
stages.done: We have a plan for the site: the zones, the power, where the gear lives, how the footage gets out, and the shift pattern.

stages.title: Central planning and gear
stages.why: We turn the site plan into a schedule, and the schedule into phones on the floor.
do: Central planning reads the dashboard: how many floors are active, when each project ends, and how many phones and workers are free.
It writes the dispatch schedule: which phones leave inventory on which day, and which site they go to.
It sends the order to procurement. Mazen provides the phones, caps, mounts, chargers, and spares, and hands them to the Portfolio Manager.
The daily hour quota and the start date go on the dashboard.
stages.done: The dispatch schedule is set, the gear is with the Portfolio Manager, and the daily quota is on the dashboard.

stages.title: Day 0
stages.why: We make sure everything works before the first real hour is filmed.
do: We set up the charging stations and the device room.
We label every phone and mount, and we test the network from the floor.
Every wearer signs the forms: a copy of their ID, the consent form, the fraud briefing, and one account in their own name.
We show every wearer the camera angle, the 30-minute cycle, and that hat off means tap stop first.
We run live pilot recordings and check them for angle and lighting.
stages.done: The pilot footage has been checked, every wearer has their papers on file, and Moharam has certified the launch.

stages.title: Filming
stages.owner: The Portfolio Manager and the operators
do: We rotate wearers so nobody films the same task all week.
We run the 30-minute cycles and restart them on time.
We enforce charging, custody, and clock-in and clock-out every day.
No phone sleeps holding more than a day of footage.
stages.done: The site hits its hours with clean footage, every day.

stages.title: Quality review
stages.owner: Youssef Medhat and the Portfolio Manager
stages.why: Nothing bad leaves the building, and we catch repeat offenders early.
do: Our own team reviews every uploaded video and decides: keep it, flag it, or delete it.
A flag reaches the Portfolio Manager the same day and the worker within 24 hours, with the fix.
Three flags pulls the worker. Two strikes pauses the device until the worker is retrained.
The month-end audit runs before we invoice anything.
stages.done: The flag rate is falling week over week, and the client has no surprises.

stages.title: Daily reporting
stages.why: We want one honest number for the whole company every night.
do: Every Portfolio Manager sends the wrap report: hours, active phones, hardware, problems, and fixes worth copying.
Mano combines them into one company view and the founders' evening number.
Adham, Moharam, and Mano review every site against its quota, move phones and people to where the hours are, and clear the day's escalations.
stages.done: The number is on the dashboard every evening.

loops.text: Filming feeds the review, and the review corrects the filming, every day.
